title: Such a fun time at the invited dress rehearsal! 👻🔮 #musicaltheatre #b...
transcript: A love song for a ouija board sung by Tony-winning legend Andrea Martin makes for a pretty great kick off to this year's Encores season. This rare revival of the musical comedy High Spirits has a pretty impressive cast, which also includes Tony-winner Katrina Lenk, Rachel Dratch, and real life married couple Phillipa Soo and Steven Pasquale. The musical is based on the Noel Coward play Blithe Spirit, which I was lucky enough to see about eleven years ago starring the great Angela Lansbury. And I don't remember the specifics of it all that well, but from what I do remember it seems like the book of this musical is relatively faithful to the play, but with some major exceptions. Firstly, for this concert adaptation, they included Noel Coward as like a narrator figure reading the stage directions. Which makes sense, because even though this production, directed by Jessica Stone, has a lot of fun staging and costumes, choreography, and even some cool magic effects, it's worth noting that this production feels more like an actual concert than some other recent Encores shows. This one's clearly not trying to go to Broadway, it's just trying to live up to the Encores mission of presenting this rare gem. But onto my favorite thing, which is that, aside from setting the action in the 60s instead of the 40s, probably the big biggest change they made from the play was adding a lot of really kooky material for the Madame Arcati character; Andrea Martin plays this psychic medium, but it's mostly a story about this guy getting haunted by the ghost of his dead wife. Meanwhile, Andrea Martin has a song about how much she loves riding bicycles. There's a love song to her ouija board, like I said, and she has two big production numbers with this entourage of beatniks that she hangs out with at a cafe. All of that was added for the musical, and at first I was like, what are we doing here? But then when they really commit to the bit, I was like, this is my favorite thing about this adaptation. As for the rest of the score, it definitely has an old school charm to it and sometimes added a nice texture to the character dynamics. But more often I found myself thinking that while the songs are nice, I’d be perfectly happy to just be watching the play instead. But they didn't detract anything really, either, and it was still fun to have this rare opportunity to see this version of it. And I do think that the comedy that serves as the backbone to the play was also executed pretty well in this musical. So if you're interested in checking out High Spirits, it's running through February 15th at City Center Encores!
